verses.text: The righteous perish, and no one lays it to heart. Merciful men are taken away, and no one considers that the righteous is taken away from the evil.
He enters into peace. They rest in their beds, each one who walks in his uprightness.
“But draw near here, you sons of a sorceress, you offspring  of adulterers and prostitutes.
Whom do you mock? Against whom do you make a wide mouth, and stick out your tongue? Aren’t you children of disobedience, and offspring  of falsehood,
you who inflame yourselves among the oaks, under every green tree; who kill the children in the valleys, under the clefts of the rocks?
Among the smooth stones of the valley is your portion; they, they are your lot. You have even poured a drink offering to them. You have offered an offering. Shall I be appeased for these things?
On a high and lofty mountain you have set your bed. You also went up there to offer sacrifice.

You have set up your memorial behind the doors and the posts; for you have exposed yourself to someone besides me, and have gone up; you have enlarged your bed, and made you a covenant with them. You loved what you saw on their bed.
You went to the king with oil, and increased your perfumes, and sent your ambassadors far off, and degraded yourself even to Sheol.
You were wearied with the length of your ways; yet you didn’t say, ‘It is in vain.’ You found a reviving of your strength; therefore you weren’t faint.
“Whom have you dreaded and feared, so that you lie, and have not remembered me, nor laid it to your heart? Haven’t I held my peace for a long time, and you don’t fear me?
I will declare your righteousness; and as for your works, they will not benefit you.

When you cry, let those whom you have gathered deliver you; but the wind will take them. a breath will carry them all away: but he who takes refuge in me will possess the land, and will inherit my holy mountain.”
He will say, “Build up, build up, prepare the way! Remove the stumbling-block out of the way of my people.”

For thus says the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also who is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.
For I will not contend forever, neither will I be always angry; for the spirit would faint before me, and the souls whom I have made.
I was angry because of the iniquity of his covetousness, and struck him; I hid myself and was angry; and he went on backsliding in the way of his heart.
I have seen his ways, and will heal him: I will lead him also, and restore comforts to him and to his mourners.
I create the fruit of the lips: Peace, peace, to him who is far off and to him who is near,” says Yahweh; “and I will heal them.”
But the wicked are like the troubled sea; for it can’t rest, and its waters cast up mire and mud.
“There is no peace”, says my God, “for the wicked.”

footnotes.content: When the righteous die, the world holds its breath for a moment, then moves on—not from cruelty, but from blindness. Yet the Lord remembers. He sees each faithful life as a rescue from the coming storm, a soul snatched to safety before darkness thickens.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: There's a quiet dignity in the death of the upright—they enter peace like a room prepared long ago. Their beds are their graves, their rest a homecoming. Jesus spoke of sleep this way too, and we learned that sleep before Him is not an ending but a gentle waking.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The daughters of disobedience—those shaped by false gods and false loves—are called to listen. Isaiah speaks as a parent calls back a child headed toward harm. The address stings because it is spoken by one who loves them still.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mockery and boasting are the first signs of a heart that has forgotten God. When we ridicule faith or jeer at the righteous, we nail down our own lies—binding ourselves tighter to what cannot save us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Oak trees and high places—these were where Israel turned to worship idols, offering what was most precious to false gods. The echo is hard: what we dedicate to lies, we pour away. Jesus alone accepts the gift of a broken heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Smooth stones in the valley—chosen as idols, hallowed by human hands. They become the inheritance of the unfaithful: a cold bargain in exchange for the living God. He asks plainly: can these dead things satisfy? Will they ever be enough?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: High mountains are where we stake our pride. We carry our beds—our deepest loves—to heights where we think God cannot see, not knowing He dwells even higher, watching not to condemn but to call us down to safety.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A memorial behind the door is a secret kept from the Lord—or so we imagine. But He sees what we hide and loves us still. The covenant made with shadows fades; only His covenant endures. He bids us take a different bed, in His light.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Oil and perfumes, gifts sent far—the language of devotion squandered on distance and darkness. Sheol is the farthest reach of our own making. Yet the Lord is not reluctant; He calls us back from the furthest place if we will listen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wearied by a long road of emptiness, and yet—without thinking—we find a second wind from our own stubborn will. We keep climbing, convinced the next false comfort will satisfy. Only when we stop and turn do we find true strength in the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fear of the world makes us lie to ourselves and to God. His long silence is not indifference; it is space He opens for us to remember Him. He asks gently: why do you not fear me, who holds all things in His hand?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He will proclaim what false righteousness we have claimed—laying it bare. Our works, empty of His presence, profit nothing. Yet this stripping away is an act of kindness: only when we see ourselves truly do we seek the only true Righteousness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wind scatters the idols we gathered. But those who flee to the Lord—who take shelter in His refuge—inherit the land and the holy mountain. The contrast is absolute: what you summon will scatter like breath, but what God gives remains forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Build, build, prepare—the Lord's command to His messengers. Remove each stone of shame, each barrier we've laid in the path. The way to His mercy is already being cleared, long before we decide to walk it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The High and Holy One, who dwells in eternity and in the broken heart—this is the great paradox of grace. He bends from the throne to sit with the humble and contrite. This is where Jesus is found, where every revival of spirit begins.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He will not contend forever—His anger is not eternal, His silence is not permanent. The souls He made are dear to Him; He cannot bear to see them faint forever. His nature is to restore, not to destroy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even His anger at our greed is a form of love—a blow that wakes us, a hidden face that makes us aware we are lost. The backsliding we choose teaches us our own weakness, and that is the first step home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He has seen our ways—every detour, every fall. And He says: I will heal. Not scold, not cast away, but heal. He leads the wanderer back and restores comfort to the brokenhearted. This is the God we meet in Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Peace, peace—spoken twice, for those far off and near. Out of His lips come both the words and the thing itself. What we sow in falsehood, He redeems through the fruit of His own words. In Jesus, this peace is made flesh for all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The wicked are like a sea that never rests—always churning, always restless, casting up mire and mud. Wickedness is not freedom; it is its own prison of perpetual unease. Only in submission to the Lord does the soul find its harbor.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No peace for the wicked—not as punishment, but as the natural fruit of their choice. The God of peace does not give peace to those who reject Him. Yet His arms remain open; the offer stands even in this final word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
